claims.text: The National Flood Insurance Program, offered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, is the most common source of flood insurance in the United States.
claims.label: the NFIP flood program

claims.text: Private flood insurance is increasingly available and can offer tailored coverage and potentially lower premiums for some homeowners.
claims.label: private flood insurance options

claims.text: The NFIP insures properties in Special Flood Hazard Areas, which FEMA designates from historical flood data and risk assessments.
claims.label: the Special Flood Hazard Areas

claims.text: A Special Flood Hazard Area has a one-percent chance of flooding in any given year and is often called the 100-year floodplain.
claims.label: the one-percent floodplain

claims.text: Flood coverage typically includes damage to the building's structure, its electrical and plumbing systems, and personal belongings, but not landscaping, detached garages or fences.
claims.label: what the policy covers

claims.text: Premiums depend on the property's elevation relative to the Base Flood Elevation, the highest level floodwater is expected to reach in a 100-year flood, and on the insured's deductible.
claims.label: how premiums are set

claims.text: Standard homeowners insurance policies generally exclude flood damage, so separate flood insurance must be purchased.
claims.label: the homeowners-policy exclusion
